title: its vs it's
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: it's = it is; its = belonging to it.

items.point: it's is short for 'it is' or 'it has'.
its shows something belongs to it (no apostrophe).

title: your vs you're
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: you're = you are; your = belonging to you.

items.point: you're is short for 'you are'.
your shows something belongs to you.

title: there vs their vs they're
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: Place, possession, and 'they are'.

items.point: there points to a place.
their shows belonging to them.
they're is short for 'they are'.

title: say vs tell
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: tell needs a person; say usually does not.

items.point: Use tell with a person (tell someone).
Use say without a person, or with 'to'.
items.example: She said hello. / He said to me...

title: do vs make
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: make = create; do = actions/tasks.

items.point: Use make when you create or produce something.
items.example: She made a cake. / make a decision.

items.point: Use do for activities and jobs.
items.example: I do my homework. / do the dishes.

title: much vs many
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: many for countable; much for uncountable.

items.point: Use many with things you can count.
items.example: How many apples do you want?

items.point: Use much with things you cannot count.
items.example: How much time do we have?

title: few vs little
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: few for countable; little for uncountable.

items.point: Use few / a few with countable nouns.
items.example: I have a few friends here.

items.point: Use little / a little with uncountable nouns.
items.example: There is a little water left.

title: since vs for
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: since = a point; for = a period.

items.point: Use since with a starting point in time.
Use for with a length of time.
items.example: I have lived here for five years.

title: affect vs effect
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: affect = verb; effect = noun.

items.point: affect is usually a verb (to change something).
effect is usually a noun (the result).
items.example: The medicine had a good effect.

title: borrow vs lend
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: borrow = take; lend = give.

items.point: You borrow something FROM someone (you take it).
You lend something TO someone (you give it).
items.example: Can you lend me your pen?

title: good vs well
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: good describes a noun; well describes a verb.

items.point: good is an adjective (describes a thing/person).
well is an adverb (describes how you do something).

title: bring vs take
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: bring = toward here; take = away from here.

items.point: Use bring for movement toward the speaker.
items.example: Please bring the book to me.

items.point: Use take for movement away from the speaker.
items.example: Take this letter to the office.

title: some vs any
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: some in positives; any in questions/negatives.

items.point: Use some in positive sentences and offers.
items.example: I have some questions. / Would you like some tea?

items.point: Use any in questions and negatives.
items.example: Do you have any money? / I don't have any.

title: learn vs teach
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: learn = get knowledge; teach = give it.

items.point: You learn something (you receive knowledge).
You teach someone (you give knowledge).

title: between vs among
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: between = two; among = three or more.

items.point: Use between for two things or people.
Use among for three or more (a group).
items.example: Share the sweets among the children.

title: rise vs raise
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: rise = go up itself; raise = lift something.

items.point: rise means to go up by itself (no object).
items.example: The sun rises in the east.

items.point: raise means to lift something up (needs an object).

title: fun vs funny
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: fun = enjoyable; funny = makes you laugh.

items.point: fun means enjoyable or pleasant.
items.example: The party was a lot of fun.

items.point: funny means it makes you laugh (or is strange).

title: advice vs advise
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: advice = noun; advise = verb.

items.point: advice is a noun (uncountable).
advise is a verb (to give advice).

title: this vs that
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: this = near; that = far.

items.point: Use this for something near you.
items.example: This is my phone (in my hand).

items.point: Use that for something farther away.

title: who vs whom
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: who = subject; whom = object.

items.point: Use who for the person doing the action.
Use whom for the person receiving the action (formal).

title: remember vs remind
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: remember yourself; remind someone.

items.point: You remember something by yourself.
You remind someone else.
items.example: Please remind me to call him.

title: hear vs listen
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: hear = by chance; listen = on purpose.

items.point: Hear happens without trying.
Listen means you pay attention.

title: travel vs trip vs journey
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: travel = general; trip/journey = one event.

items.point: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable).
A trip or journey is one particular event.
items.example: We had a nice trip to Goa.

title: lay vs lie
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: lay needs an object; lie does not.

items.point: Lay means to put something down (needs an object).
items.example: Lay the book on the table.

items.point: Lie means to rest / be in a position (no object).

title: win vs beat
subtitle: Which word to use
tip: win a game/prize; beat a person/team.

items.point: You win a match, a prize, or a game.
You beat an opponent.
